anchor.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must recognize, and not report, a #[cfg(unix)] transport or adapter function or match arm that sits beside a loopback TCP enum variant or function with no #[cfg] guard, which Windows uses instead.
anchor.scope: The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item in crates/sc-lint-portability.

item.title: Sprint MS9: PORT-011 path separators
item.text: Add a new portability rule PORT-011 in crates/sc-lint-portability that reports hard-coded '/' path separators in string literals passed to std::fs functions.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor about sc-lint's PORT-010 rule, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work in `item.text` change which `#[cfg(unix)]` items PORT-010 reports, or depend directly on such a change? Judge subject overlap only; do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or directly depends on when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` item, whatever sibling shape it handles.
criteria.no: The item changes a different rule, a different feature, or something other than when PORT-010 reports `#[cfg(unix)]` items, even if it is in the same crate.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions PORT-010 or portability linting but it is not possible to tell whether it changes which `#[cfg(unix)]` items PORT-010 reports.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for PORT-010 to stop reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item when a loopback TCP sibling with no `#[cfg]` guard, used by Windows, sits beside it? A generic mention of PORT-010 false positives, or a different sibling shape, does not count. Judge presence of this plan only, not conflict.

criteria.yes: The item says PORT-010 stops reporting, skips, or treats as covered a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm because an unguarded loopback TCP enum variant or function beside it serves Windows.
criteria.no: The item does not say this: it is silent about an unguarded loopback TCP sibling, handles a different sibling shape, speaks only generally, or says PORT-010 keeps reporting the item.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions a loopback TCP sibling and PORT-010 but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 is to stop reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` say that PORT-010 keeps reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item even though an unguarded loopback TCP sibling beside it serves Windows? Silence about this shape, or work on a different shape, is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item says PORT-010 keeps reporting, still reports, or is left unchanged for a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item that has an unguarded loopback TCP sibling serving Windows.
criteria.no: The item does not say PORT-010 keeps reporting that shape: it plans to stop reporting it, is silent about it, or handles a different shape.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions the shape but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 will keep reporting it.
